column1: # Long-horizon variance ratios of the CRSP US market total return, on `uni.apps.MarketSim.varianceRatio`'s
# definition: vr(q) = Var(non-overlapping q-session sums) / (q * Var(daily)), sample variances (n-1),
# LOG daily returns, series truncated to a whole number of blocks. On the file as printed, the
# vr20/vr60 columns REPRODUCE persistence-2026-08-29.tsv's c-rows to the third decimal, which is this
# file's control: the same pipeline, re-run 2026-08-30 from the 202606-vintage
# F-F_Research_Data_Factors_daily (Mkt-RF + RF). (persistence-2026-09-02.tsv re-measured those c-rows
# with the twins' own functions and reads 1.169 / 1.175 at c1926 against this pipeline's 1.166 / 1.143;
# that pipeline's construction was not recorded and could not be reproduced. The negative the rows
# settle does not depend on the third decimal.) The rows below are read LAG-FREE, on a `record_bands
# -unlagged` copy of the file: the daily returns through 1999-03-10 with the stale-price lag removed,
# an MA(2) inversion fitted per calendar five-year block (`unlag_returns`).
# WHY THIS FILE SETTLES A NEGATIVE. The 60d variance-ratio row is blind past its own horizon, and the
# 0.22.1 disaster channel moved the model's century-path vr(5y) from 0.89 to 1.15 unwatched. These
# columns were measured to anchor that horizon and CANNOT: the record's long-horizon readings are
# era-split with the sign flipping between windows (vr1260: 0.623 for the century, 0.997 post-1954,
# and a window of n non-overlapping blocks carries relative noise ~ sqrt(2/(n-1)) — 32% for the
# century's 20 five-year blocks, 39% for c1954's 14 — so no window pins a value the model's own
# per-century spread (p5-p95 roughly 0.45-2.9) does not already contain. The model's 1.15 sits
# INSIDE the record on both horizons. NO GATED ROW is derived from this file; it exists so the next
# person who reaches for "the record mean-reverts at five years" (Poterba-Summers, measured here as
# the c1926 row only) finds the era-split and the block noise beside the number.
# nblocks(q) = sessions div q for the vr1260 column, stated because it IS the precision.
